speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing this pruritic rash and if the lesions are flat or raised?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the fever preceding the rash and the facial involvement sparing the nose, have you noticed any joint pain, swollen glands, or a "sandpaper" texture to the skin?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (caused by Group A Streptococcus).

The prior diagnosis of Pyelonephritis is incorrect; that condition does not present with a pruritic rash or rhinorrhea. Please confirm if your daughter has a history of sore throat and has not been treated with antibiotics recently.
